tone_statements.citation: Yang, Wenjing & Cathryn Yang. 2018. Reduction in Dali Nisu tone change-in-progress. In Proceedings of the 6th International Symposium on Tonal Aspects of Languages (TAL 2018), Berlin, 18-20 June 2018, 46-50. ISCA. doi:10.21437/TAL.2018-10.
tone_statements.quote: Dali Nisu is a previously undocumented Ngwi (Loloish, Tibeto-Burman) language spoken in Dali Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China. There are approximately 20,000 speakers; [...] In Dali Nisu, each syllable is specified for one of four tone categories: high level (55), mid level (33), low falling (21) and low rising (13). The purpose of this study is to test four hypotheses about reduction changes in Nisu: 1) the high level tone (Tone 55) is lowering, 2) the low rising tone (Tone 13) is flattening, 3) the low falling tone (Tone 21) is also flattening, and 4) the overall tonal range is decreasing.
tone_statements.locator: p. 46, Section 2 'Apparent-time study of Dali Nisu tone change-in-progress' (first paragraph)
tone_statements.summary: Four lexical tones on the syllable - high level 55, mid level 33, low falling 21, low rising 13 - with ongoing reduction (55 lowering, 13 and 21 flattening); no stress statement.

sources.quote: Dali Nisu is a previously undocumented Ngwi (Loloish, Tibeto-Burman) language spoken in Dali Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China. There are approximately 20,000 speakers; [...] In Dali Nisu, each syllable is specified for one of four tone categories: high level (55), mid level (33), low falling (21) and low rising (13). The purpose of this study is to test four hypotheses about reduction changes in Nisu: 1) the high level tone (Tone 55) is lowering, 2) the low rising tone (Tone 13) is flattening, 3) the low falling tone (Tone 21) is also flattening, and 4) the overall tonal range is decreasing.
sources.locator: p. 46, Section 2 'Apparent-time study of Dali Nisu tone change-in-progress' (first paragraph)
sources.note: First-hand acoustic study (26 speakers, 66 words, Praat F0, LME models): Dali Nisu is a syllable-tone language with four lexical tone categories 55, 33, 21, 13 (tone-bearing unit = the vowel); apparent-time changes in progress: 55 lowering (partly overlapping 33 in young speakers), 13 and 21 flattening, tonal range shrinking; initial-consonant voicing interacts with the changes; Standard-Mandarin schooling as a factor. Figures 2-3 give normalized tone plots for an 85-year-old and an 18-year-old speaker.
